sources.entry: Toggl Desktop - Toggl Desktop app for Windows, Mac and Linux.

summary.one_liner: Toggl Desktop is the native desktop time tracking client for Toggl for macOS, Windows and Linux, now superseded by rewritten apps and no longer accepting feature pull requests.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Toggl Desktop as a native desktop client for the Toggl time tracking service, with helper features such as idle detection, reminders to track time, and a Pomodoro timer. It links to prebuilt downloads for macOS (dmg and Mac App Store), Windows (installers, Chocolatey, Microsoft Store) and Linux (tarball and Flathub). It also gives build instructions for macOS (Xcode and CocoaPods), Linux (CMake with Qt 5.12+) and Windows (Visual Studio 2019). The project status notice says the maintainers rewrote the macOS and Windows apps and will no longer implement or accept new features here. The README does not state a license.
use_cases: track time with a desktop app for Toggl
use a Pomodoro timer while tracking work
get idle detection and reminders to track time
build Toggl Desktop from source on macOS, Windows or Linux
install a Toggl time tracker from Flathub, Chocolatey or Microsoft Store
how_to_run: Linux: sudo apt install libxss-dev build-essential libgl-dev libreadline-dev
macOS: sudo gem install bundler, then make init_cocoapods, then open src/ui/osx/TogglDesktop.xcworkspace in Xcode and build the TogglDesktop scheme
Windows: open src\ui\windows\TogglDesktop\TogglDesktop.sln in Visual Studio 2019 and run in Debug mode
notable: Native apps for macOS, Windows and Linux built on a shared C++ core with Qt for Linux
Built-in idle detection, track reminders and Pomodoro timer
Official builds distributed through Mac App Store, Microsoft Store, Chocolatey and Flathub
Builds target a testing server by default; live-server setup is covered by a separate guide
caveats: Superseded: maintainers will no longer implement or accept pull requests for new features
Linux builds support 64-bit only; macOS officially supports 10.11 and newer
Windows app was tested on Windows 7, 8, 8.1 and 10 only; not tested on Surface-type touchscreens
